jobs.title: Housing Specialist
jobs.description:
A national housing consulting firm that manages Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) program operations on behalf of public housing authorities is hiring a Housing Specialist for its onsite Chicago office. This is a client-facing role at the center of how families and property owners interact with a federally funded rental assistance program: determining eligibility, calculating rent and assistance payments, processing recertifications, and resolving issues between tenants, landlords, and the housing authority. The office runs a high-volume, in-person walk-in day each week alongside a full slate of scheduled appointments, so the role rewards someone who stays calm, organized, and solution-focused under steady public contact. This seat offers direct exposure to federal housing policy in practice, a structured 90-day onboarding plan, and a clear path to more responsibility for someone who performs.

Anticipated $45,000-$50,000 per year, based on experience level and credentials
Benefits include: Health, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with Roth option, Employee Assistance Program, employer-paid life/AD&D insurance
PTO, paid personal days, paid holidays, and pet insurance
Full-time, Monday-Friday, onsite schedule (8:30 AM-5:00 PM); this is an in-office role with no hybrid or remote component

Overview

Determine and document program eligibility, household income, and rent calculations for applicants and current participants
Process annual and interim recertifications on schedule and keep participant files audit-ready
Manage move and portability paperwork so transitions between units or jurisdictions happen without unnecessary disruption
Serve as a front-line point of contact for a high volume of in-person visitors, including a dedicated weekly walk-in day
Mediate issues between tenants, property owners, and the housing authority, aiming for fair, well-documented outcomes
Maintain accurate records and correct quality-control findings on your own work

Preferred Skills and Experience

High school diploma or GED, required
Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program credential, preferred
1 or more years of experience in a client-facing customer service role, required
1 or more years of experience in government eligibility determination or a similar rental/lease-up field, required
1 or more years of experience specifically within an HCV program, preferred
Strongly Preferred — bilingual in Spanish or another commonly used language
Comfortable in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, SharePoint) and able to pick up new case-management software quickly
Able to pass a background check and drug screen

jobs.description:

Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

Our research in Alzheimer's disease aims to identify genetic factors associated with dementia, specifically Alzheimer's type. We are focused on increasing the representation of our study population by enrolling individuals from various ancestries. Through this, we seek to better understand the genetic underpinnings of memory loss and dementia. By collecting comprehensive data and biological samples, we will conduct genetic studies to identify potential genetic markers for dementia. The Program Manager will play a key role in managing these efforts, including participant recruitment, enrollment, and data oversight, while collaborating with study sites to ensure the success of recruitment and data collection initiatives. This is a full-time, 1 year term position.

Essential Functions

Identify and enroll eligible individuals and meet enrollment goals. Cultivate relationships with potential study participants; providing education, building trust and promoting interest in study activities. Work within human research protection processes: create and maintain appropriate protocol documents, confidentially and sensitively obtain and review family and medical histories and perform study specific interviews, instruments, and exams and identify, obtain and review appropriate medical records. Draw blood for genetic studies (training can be provided on the job). Prepare detailed participant exam reports for adjudication. Oversee and maintain complete research files and comprehensive databases including: consent forms, demographics, family and medical history forms and all other study specific forms and data. Document and maintain records to show effort that may not be reflected in enrollment numbers; events attended, sign-ups, declines, phone calls, messages left, etc. Ensure compliance with IRB approved protocols and maintain data integrity. (70%)
Collaborate with study leadership to create strategic approaches to identify and engage community and clinic partnerships. Build community partnerships through effective outreach efforts. Develop and implement community recruitment strategy and methods. Design and manage community events; reach out to various groups including but not limited to the Alzheimer's association, churches, community senior centers, social groups and caregiver support groups. Maintain open communication with physicians and office staff participating in the studies in the community. Working closely with the research staff, monitor and oversee research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment and enrollment of study participants for the DAWN study and ensure timelines and goals are met. Evaluate outreach efforts, identify areas for improvement, advise leadership of alternative methods/efforts, and implement adjustments. (10%)
Facilitate communication and provide regular research updates for meetings. Work with the team to prepare a yearly participant newsletter. Participate in research group meetings locally and with the national network and communicate with the Research Project Director and Principal Investigators to ensure that work on the studies is being performed as needed and expected. Attend regular meetings locally and nationally with the principal investigators/coordinators and collaborators. Maintain open communication/collaboration between departments within and outside of institution. (10%)
Provide training and instruction regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others working on the study. (7%)

Nonessential Functions

May serve as a co-author on research publications. (1%)
Provide training regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others who work with the studies. May supervise students and technicians. (1%)
Perform other duties as assigned. (1%)

CONTACTS

Department: On-going contact with supervisor. Contact with Research Project Director and PI as needed, staff, faculty, postdocs, and study participants. Will work closely with any other team members who work on the same study, coordinate research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment, and enrollment of study participants for the human genetics research studies in their area.

University: Contact as needed with purchasing, human resources, space, and facilities planning, environmental health, safety/contact, Research Administration, IRB, and Sponsored Projects Accounting.

External: Regular contact with community leaders, collaborators at other universities, institutions, and industry. Occasional contact with vendors.

Students: On-going contact with students.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

This position has no direct supervision of staff employees. May train new staff; direct the work of students.

Qualifications

Experience 2 to 5 years of experience with minority community and familiarity with the aging population, preferably in the Cleveland area;

Education: Bachelor's degree required. Prefer Nursing degree. Must have and maintain a valid driver's license and be able to travel to participant homes, exam locations and community events, primarily within the local area.

Required Skills

Ability to concisely and effectively communicate methods, concepts, and study designs to all groups as appropriate, relevant and indicated.
Effective and professional interpersonal skills. Demonstrated expertise and strong leadership skills in team-oriented environment.
Ability to facilitate open communication/collaboration between department and other areas, as well as open communication with physicians and office staff participating in the studies in the community.
Maintain level of confidentiality commensurate with nature of involvement with study participants, medical records and other sensitive HIPAA, demographic and family history information.
Good problem solving and decision-making skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated willingness to be hands-on and pro-active.
Ability to multitask, work independently, and set own priorities, while maintaining accuracy and attention to details.
Ability to work effectively with internal and external colleagues and collaborators. Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Ability to meet consistent attendance.
Phlebotomy skills preferred, but training will be provided to attain those skills.
Ability to demonstrate successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest.
Willingness to learn and work with artificial intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Occasional national/international travel for collaborative meetings. May need to work on occasional weekends and during evenings to attend and participate in community/recruitment events.

Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary range available for this position at the time of its posting. The salary range is between $49,257 and $62,311, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.

Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

Our research in Alzheimer's disease aims to identify genetic factors associated with dementia, specifically Alzheimer's type. We are focused on increasing the representation of our study population by enrolling individuals from various ancestries. Through this, we seek to better understand the genetic underpinnings of memory loss and dementia. By collecting comprehensive data and biological samples, we will conduct genetic studies to identify potential genetic markers for dementia. The Program Manager will play a key role in managing these efforts, including participant recruitment, enrollment, and data oversight, while collaborating with study sites to ensure the success of recruitment and data collection initiatives. This is a full-time, 1 year term position.

Essential Functions

Identify and enroll eligible individuals and meet enrollment goals. Cultivate relationships with potential study participants; providing education, building trust and promoting interest in study activities. Work within human research protection processes: create and maintain appropriate protocol documents, confidentially and sensitively obtain and review family and medical histories and perform study specific interviews, instruments, and exams and identify, obtain and review appropriate medical records. Draw blood for genetic studies (training can be provided on the job). Prepare detailed participant exam reports for adjudication. Oversee and maintain complete research files and comprehensive databases including: consent forms, demographics, family and medical history forms and all other study specific forms and data. Document and maintain records to show effort that may not be reflected in enrollment numbers; events attended, sign-ups, declines, phone calls, messages left, etc. Ensure compliance with IRB approved protocols and maintain data integrity. (70%)
Collaborate with study leadership to create strategic approaches to identify and engage community and clinic partnerships. Build community partnerships through effective outreach efforts. Develop and implement community recruitment strategy and methods. Design and manage community events; reach out to various groups including but not limited to the Alzheimer's association, churches, community senior centers, social groups and caregiver support groups. Maintain open communication with physicians and office staff participating in the studies in the community. Working closely with the research staff, monitor and oversee research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment and enrollment of study participants for the DAWN study and ensure timelines and goals are met. Evaluate outreach efforts, identify areas for improvement, advise leadership of alternative methods/efforts, and implement adjustments. (10%)
Facilitate communication and provide regular research updates for meetings. Work with the team to prepare a yearly participant newsletter. Participate in research group meetings locally and with the national network and communicate with the Research Project Director and Principal Investigators to ensure that work on the studies is being performed as needed and expected. Attend regular meetings locally and nationally with the principal investigators/coordinators and collaborators. Maintain open communication/collaboration between departments within and outside of institution. (10%)
Provide training and instruction regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others working on the study. (7%)

Nonessential Functions

May serve as a co-author on research publications. (1%)
Provide training regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others who work with the studies. May supervise students and technicians. (1%)
Perform other duties as assigned. (1%)

CONTACTS

Department: On-going contact with supervisor. Contact with Research Project Director and PI as needed, staff, faculty, postdocs, and study participants. Will work closely with any other team members who work on the same study, coordinate research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment, and enrollment of study participants for the human genetics research studies in their area.

University: Contact as needed with purchasing, human resources, space, and facilities planning, environmental health, safety/contact, Research Administration, IRB, and Sponsored Projects Accounting.

External: Regular contact with community leaders, collaborators at other universities, institutions, and industry. Occasional contact with vendors.

Students: On-going contact with students.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

This position has no direct supervision of staff employees. May train new staff; direct the work of students.

Qualifications

Experience 2 to 5 years of experience with minority community and familiarity with the aging population, preferably in the Cleveland area;

Education: Bachelor's degree required. Prefer Nursing degree. Must have and maintain a valid driver's license and be able to travel to participant homes, exam locations and community events, primarily within the local area.

Required Skills

Ability to concisely and effectively communicate methods, concepts, and study designs to all groups as appropriate, relevant and indicated.
Effective and professional interpersonal skills. Demonstrated expertise and strong leadership skills in team-oriented environment.
Ability to facilitate open communication/collaboration between department and other areas, as well as open communication with physicians and office staff participating in the studies in the community.
Maintain level of confidentiality commensurate with nature of involvement with study participants, medical records and other sensitive HIPAA, demographic and family history information.
Good problem solving and decision-making skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated willingness to be hands-on and pro-active.
Ability to multitask, work independently, and set own priorities, while maintaining accuracy and attention to details.
Ability to work effectively with internal and external colleagues and collaborators. Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Ability to meet consistent attendance.
Phlebotomy skills preferred, but training will be provided to attain those skills.
Ability to demonstrate successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest.
Willingness to learn and work with artificial intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Normal office environment. Employee will need to drive a personal vehicle to participants¿ home and exam locations and community events. (approximately 50%-75% of travel required). Occasional national/international travel for collaborative meetings. May need to work on occasional weekends and during evenings to attend and participate in community/recruitment events.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

Working under general supervision, the Research Assistant 2 will plan and carry out the laboratory's research program by conducting molecular, biochemical, and cell biology experiments. This position will contribute to studies of the molecular mechanisms underlying innate immune protein function, including the use of chimeric proteins to identify key determinants of antimicrobial activity through biochemical, biophysical, structural, and cell biology approaches. Primary responsibilities include performing laboratory experiments, analyzing and documenting research data, maintaining laboratory operations and equipment, and assisting with manuscript and grant preparation. This position supports the laboratory's research mission by generating high-quality experimental data and ensuring the efficient operation of ongoing research projects.

Essential Functions

Plan and carry out experiments according to specific instructions. Perform cell culture, protein expression and purification, quantitative analysis of confocal images on protein-bacteria interactions, molecular cloning, stable cell line making, SDS-PAGE, western blotting, and other related assays. (50%)
Conduct a series of research experiments to supply scientific information as part of a larger project, in collaboration with lab staff, and assist the principal investigator. May conduct specific experiments and tasks independently. Troubleshoot protocols, provide interpretation of data and may assist in developing improved techniques, projection methods or procedures. (20%)
Collect and analyze data to contribute to collaborative projects. Maintain detailed laboratory records, prepare publication-quality figures, summarize findings, and assist with manuscript and grant preparation. (10%)
Maintain laboratory equipment, organize reagents and biological samples. Manage laboratory inventory and coordinate ordering of research supplies. (6%)
Train undergraduate students and new laboratory staff in standard laboratory operations, maintenance, techniques, and safety procedures; direct the work of students. (10%)

Nonessential Functions

Perform other duties as assigned. (4%)

CONTACTS

Department: Daily contact with supervisor to discuss research and maintain workflow.

University: Occasional contact with other departments to share information.

External: Limited or no contact with vendors to exchange information.

Students: Contact with student employees to exchange information.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

This position has no direct supervision of staff employees. May assist in training new staff and students on lab operations and maintenance.

Qualifications

Education/Experience: Bachelor's degree and 1 to 3 years of experience or Associate's degree in an approved biotechnology program and 2 to 4 years of experience required.

Required Skills

Knowledge of commonly-used concepts, practices, and procedures in life sciences. Experience with bacterial and mammalian cell culture, protein expression and purification, molecular cloning, and Western blotting.
Background in biophysics, biochemistry, cell biology and structural biology, any of above field.

Ability to operate laboratory equipment.

General laboratory environment. May involve handling chemicals, recombinant DNA, cell cultures, and laboratory instrumentation in accordance with institutional safety regulations. Personal protective equipment, including lab coat, gloves and goggles, will be provided to limit exposure to hazards.
